title: Overseas visitors to the UK for different purposes
prompt: The line graph shows the number of overseas visitors who came to the UK for different purposes between 1989 and 2009. Summarize the information by reporting the main features and making comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates how many individuals visited the UK for three different purposes from 1989 to 2009.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all three categories experienced a general upward trend throughout the given period, with holiday visitors exhibiting the most substantial fluctuations. Additionally, holiday travel remained the most popular purpose for most of the timeframe, while visits to friends or relatives showed the most significant growth over the two decades.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the initial figures in 1989, holiday was the most common purpose of travel with approximately 6.5 million visitors, closely followed by business trips at around 5 million. In contrast, meeting friends and relatives was considerably less popular, with only about 3.5 million visitors, which was roughly half the number of holiday travelers and 1.5 million fewer than those traveling for business purposes.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the subsequent years, the number of holiday visitors rose sharply to reach a peak of about 9 million in 1994, then decreased to around 6.5 million in 2004, before rising again to approximately 9 million in 2009. Meanwhile, business travel decreased slightly to approximately 4 million in 1994, then rose significantly to reach its peak of roughly 8 million in 2004, before dropping slightly to about 7 million by 2009. As for people visiting friends and relatives, this category reached approximately 7 million in 2004, before decreasing slightly to around 6 million by 2009.
